def is_not_prime(n: int) -> bool:
    """Return True if n is not prime, otherwise return False."""
    
    # 0 and 1 are neither prime nor composite (not considered non-prime in this context for primality tests usually starting at 2)
    # However, strictly speaking, they are "non-primes". 
    # Based on the test case `assert is_not_prime(2) == False`, we know:
    # - 2 is prime -> returns False (meaning it IS a prime number).
    
    if n <= 1:
        return True   # 0 and 1 are not prime numbers
    
    # Check divisibility from 2 up to sqrt(n)
    i = 2
    while i * i <= n:
        if n % i == 0:
            return True  # Found a divisor, so it's NOT prime (i.e., non-prime)
        i += 1
    
    return False  # No divisors found, so it IS prime


# Test cases based on your requirement and common edge cases
assert is_not_prime(2) == False   # 2 is prime -> not a "non-prime" number
assert is_not_prime(4) == True    # 4 is divisible by 2 -> non-prime
assert is_not_prime(17) == False  # 17 is prime
assert is_not_prime(9) == True    # 9 is divisible by 3
